title: Guru Nanak warns Babur that a boon can be withdrawn

blocks.text: Guru Nanak answers Babur by explaining that a boon can be withdrawn when the recipient proves unworthy of preserving it. Gifts received freely carry obligations, and divine favor does not remain with rulers who violate the moral terms under which it was granted.

He then turns prophetic and tells Babur that Mughal sovereignty will be revoked if his descendants persecute the later Gurus. Babur folds his hands in protest, insisting that his house reveres the Guru and that such betrayal should not come from his line.

The narrative immediately begins to test that claim by turning toward the later emperors. The page pivots from Babur's plea to the historical record of how Jahangir and his successors will be judged through their treatment of the Sikh Gurus.
